biography.plain_text: Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad Al Thani was Qatar's sixth ruler, serving as Amir from 1972 to 1995. A member of the Al Thani dynasty, he became head of security affairs in his teens. He later served as the country's first education minister, heir apparent, finance minister and prime minister before taking power.

long_biography.plain_text:
Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad Al Thani helped carry Qatar from protected status into independence, announcing the end of the Anglo-Qatari treaty in 1971. He also administered the new foreign-affairs portfolio as the state joined the Arab League and United Nations.

As Amir, Khalifa reorganised the cabinet and amended the interim constitution, defining roles for an Advisory Council, state budgets and public audit. His government expanded schools and colleges, founded Qatar's first university and national museum, and concluded energy-production agreements. North Field gas production began before his rule ended in 1995.
